body.en: AP Calculus BC is a comprehensive, college-level single-variable calculus curriculum equivalent to two full semesters of university calculus (Calculus I and Calculus II). It encompasses all AP Calculus AB content (Differential and Integral Calculus, Units 1–8) alongside advanced integration techniques, Euler's method, logistic differential equations, planar parametric curves, 2D vector kinematics, polar functions, and infinite sequences and series.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (AP Calculus BC Exam Format & Units Overview)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (AP التفاضل والتكامل BC Exam Format & Units Overview)

body.en:
Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

label.ar: Level 1 (Foundations) — مثال محلول · Subscore & Raw Composite Calculation

body.en:
Problem: On the AP Calculus BC exam, a student answers 36 of 45 MCQs correctly and earns 38 out of 54 points on the Free Response section. Calculate the student's composite score out of 108, and explain how the AB Subscore is isolated from these items.

Step 1 · MCQ Scaling: Each MCQ has equal weight. The Section I score is \(36 \times 1.2 = 43.2\) points.

Step 2 · FRQ Scaling: Each FRQ question is worth 9 raw points (total 54 raw points). The Section II score is \(38 \times 1.0 = 38.0\) points.

Step 3 · Composite Score: Total composite is \(43.2 + 38.0 = 81.2\) out of 108 (approx. \(75.2\%\)), which solidly falls into the 5 score range (historical cutoff is typically 64–68 out of 108).

Step 4 · AB Subscore Extraction: The College Board isolates all questions that assess AB content (approximately 27 of 45 MCQs and 3.5 of 6 FRQs, accounting for \(\sim 60\%\) of the exam). A dedicated composite score is tabulated exclusively from these items to assign the AB Subscore.

label.en: Worked Example \(B\) — AP Calculus BC Exam Format & Units Overview (Medium Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(B\) — AP التفاضل والتكامل BC Exam Format & Units Overview (Medium Application)

body.en:
Problem (Medium): Consider the infinite series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{n^p}{5^n} \). The series converges if and only if the parameter \( p \) satisfies which of the following conditions? Use the Ratio Test to determine the interval of convergence.

Step-by-Step Solution: We apply the Ratio Test. Let \( a_n = \frac{n^p}{5^n} \). Then \( a_{n+1} = \frac{(n+1)^p}{5^{n+1}} \). We compute the limit of the ratio of consecutive terms: \[ L = \lim_{n \to \infty} \left| \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} \right| = \lim_{n \to \infty} \left| \frac{(n+1)^p}{5^{n+1}} \cdot \frac{5^n}{n^p} \right| \] \[ L = \lim_{n \to \infty} \left| \frac{1}{5} \left( \frac{n+1}{n} \right)^p \right| = \lim_{n \to \infty} \left| \frac{1}{5} \left( 1 + \frac{1}{n} \right)^p \right| \] As \( n \to \infty \), \( \frac{1}{n} \to 0 \), so \( \left( 1 + \frac{1}{n} \right)^p \to 1^p = 1 \) for any real \( p \). Thus, \[ L = \frac{1}{5} \cdot 1 = \frac{1}{5} \]. According to the Ratio Test, the series converges if \( L < 1 \). Since \( L = \frac{1}{5} < 1 \) for all real values of \( p \), the series converges for all real values of \( p \).
body.ar:
Problem (Medium): Consider the infinite المتسلسلة \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{n^p}{5^n} \). The المتسلسلة converges if and only if the المعامل \( p \) satisfies which of the following conditions? Use the Ratio Test to حدّد interval of convergence.

Step-by-Step الحل: We apply the Ratio Test. Let \( a_n = \frac{n^p}{5^n} \). Then \( a_{n+1} = \frac{(n+1)^p}{5^{n+1}} \). We compute the النهاية of the ratio of consecutive terms: \[ L = \lim_{n \to \infty} \left| \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} \right| = \lim_{n \to \infty} \left| \frac{(n+1)^p}{5^{n+1}} \cdot \frac{5^n}{n^p} \right| \] \[ L = \lim_{n \to \infty} \left| \frac{1}{5} \left( \frac{n+1}{n} \right)^p \right| = \lim_{n \to \infty} \left| \frac{1}{5} \left( 1 + \frac{1}{n} \right)^p \right| \] As \( n \to \infty \), \( \frac{1}{n} \to 0 \), so \( \left( 1 + \frac{1}{n} \right)^p \to 1^p = 1 \) for any real \( p \). وعليه, \[ L = \frac{1}{5} \cdot 1 = \frac{1}{5} \]. According to the Ratio Test, the المتسلسلة converges if \( L < 1 \). Since \( L = \frac{1}{5} < 1 \) for all real values of \( p \), the المتسلسلة converges for all real values of \( p \).

label.en: ⚠️ Common Exam Traps — AP Calculus BC Exam Format & Units Overview
label.ar: ⚠️ أخطاء شائعة في الاختبار — AP التفاضل والتكامل BC Exam Format & Units Overview

body.en:
1. Adding Successive Percentages or Averaging Speeds Arithmetically: On College Board AP Calculus BC, a \(20\%\) discount followed by a \(20\%\) increase gives \(0.80 \times 1.20 = 0.96\) (a net \(4\%\) loss, not \(0\%\)). Likewise, average speed for a round trip at \(40\) and \(60\text{ km/h}\) is \(\dfrac{2(40)(60)}{100} = 48\text{ km/h}\), never \(50\text{ km/h}\).

2. Failing to Flip the Inequality Sign When Multiplying/Dividing by a Negative: In \(-5x + 7 \le 12\), dividing by \(-5\) strictly reverses \(\le\) to \(\ge\).

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — The Four Approved Graphing Calculator Capabilities

body.en: On Sections I Part B and II Part A, students are tested on their ability to use a graphing calculator efficiently. The College Board allows only four capabilities to replace analytic pencil-and-paper algebra. Any other operation (e.g. symbolic limits, symbolic integration, algebraic factoring) must be supported with complete analytic steps.

label.en: ● The Four Permitted Calculator Operations on AP Calculus BC
label.ar: ● The Four Permitted Calculator Operations on AP التفاضل والتكامل BC

body.en:
• 1. Plotting the graph of a function: Visualizing roots, local extrema, and intersection points within an arbitrary viewing window.
  • 2. Finding roots and intersection points: Numerically solving equations of the form \(f(x) = 0\) or \(f(x) = g(x)\).
  • 3. Computing numerical derivatives: Calculating \(f'(a)\) at a specific point (e.g., nDeriv(f(x), x, a)).
  • 4. Evaluating numerical definite integrals: Computing \(\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\) numerically (e.g., fnInt(f(x), x, a, b)).

Mandatory AP Protocol: You MUST write the mathematical setup on your paper before entering numbers into the calculator. Writing a numerical answer alone without an integral or derivative setup yields zero credit for that step.

• 1. Plotting the التمثيل البياني of a الدالة: Visualizing roots, local extrema, and التقاطع points within an arbitrary viewing window.

label.en: Level 2 (Medium) — Worked Example · Calculator Justification Protocol
label.ar: Level 2 (Medium) — مثال محلول · Calculator Justification Protocol

body.en:
Problem: A particle moves along a polar curve \(r = 3 + 2\cos(\theta)\) for \(0 \le \theta \le \pi\). On Section II Part A (Calculator Active), a student is asked to find the total area enclosed by the curve in the upper half-plane. Write the exact mathematical justification required by College Board readers to earn full credit.

Step 1 · Identify the Formula: The polar area formula is: \[ A = \frac{1}{2} \int_\alpha^\beta [r(\theta)]^2\,d\theta. \]

Step 2 · Write the Integral Setup: On the exam paper, write: \[ \text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \int_0^\pi (3 + 2\cos\theta)^2\,d\theta. \] (This written expression earns the 1st point: the setup point.)

Step 3 · Numerical Computation: Use the calculator's numerical integration function: \[ A = \frac{1}{2}(34.5575) \approx 17.2787... \]

Step 4 · Rounding to 3 Decimals: State the answer rounded or truncated to 3 decimal places: \[ \mathbf{17.279} \quad \text{or} \quad \mathbf{17.278}. \] (This earns the 2nd point: the answer point.)

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced / AP FRQ — The 9-Point Rubric Standard & Common Scoring Traps

body.en: Each of the 6 Free-Response Questions is graded on an exact 9-point analytic rubric by trained AP readers. Points are allocated to individual mathematical steps: setup, differential equation separation, antiderivative evaluation, constant of integration evaluation, and final justified conclusion.
body.ar: Each of the 6 Free-Response Questions is graded on an exact 9-point analytic rubric by trained AP readers. Points are allocated to individual mathematical steps: setup, المعادلة التفاضلية separation, antiderivative evaluation, الثابت of integration evaluation, and final justified conclusion.

label.en: ● The Four Fatal FRQ Traps in AP Calculus BC
label.ar: ● The Four Fatal FRQ Traps in AP التفاضل والتكامل BC

body.en:
1. Failure to Separate Variables: In any differential equation FRQ (typically 5–6 points out of 9), if the student does not explicitly separate variables as the very first step (e.g. \(\frac{1}{y}\,dy = kx\,dx\)), the student is ineligible for all subsequent points on that part, scoring 0 out of 5 or 6.
  2. Omitting the Constant of Integration \(+C\): Writing an antiderivative without \(+C\) immediately disqualifies the student from earning points for using the initial condition and finding the particular solution.
  3. Bald Answers: Writing a final numerical value without the integral, derivative, or algebraic setup earns 0 points for that question part.
  4. Failure to Justify Theorem Hypotheses: When invoking the Mean Value Theorem (MVT), Extreme Value Theorem (EVT), or Intermediate Value Theorem (IVT), failing to explicitly state that \(f(x)\) is continuous on \([a, b]\) and differentiable on \((a, b)\) forfeits the justification point.
body.ar:
1. Failure to Separate المتغيرات: In any المعادلة التفاضلية FRQ (typically 5–6 points out of 9), if the student does not explicitly separate المتغيرات as the very first step (e.g. \(\frac{1}{y}\,dy = kx\,dx\)), the student is ineligible for all subsequent points on that part, scoring 0 out of 5 or 6.
  2. Omitting the الثابت of Integration \(+C\): Writing an antiderivative without \(+C\) immediately disqualifies the student from earning points for using the initial condition and finding the particular الحل.
  3. Bald Answers: Writing a final numerical value without the التكامل, المشتقة, or algebraic setup earns 0 points for that question part.
  4. Failure to Justify مبرهنة Hypotheses: عندما invoking the Mean Value مبرهنة (MVT), Extreme Value مبرهنة (EVT), or Intermediate Value مبرهنة (IVT), failing to explicitly state that \(f(x)\) is continuous on \([a, b]\) and differentiable on \((a, b)\) forfeits the justification point.

label.en: Level 3 (Advanced/FRQ) — Worked Example · Rubric Point Breakdown
label.ar: Level 3 (Advanced/FRQ) — مثال محلول · Rubric Point Breakdown

body.en:
FRQ Prompt: Consider the differential equation \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{x(y - 1)}{2}\) with initial condition \(y(0) = 3\). Find the particular solution \(y = f(x)\).

Rubric Point 1 · Separation of Variables (1 pt): \[ \frac{1}{y - 1}\,dy = \frac{x}{2}\,dx. \]

Rubric Point 2 · Antiderivatives (2 pts): 1 pt for left side, 1 pt for right side: \[ \ln|y - 1| = \frac{x^2}{4} + C. \]

Rubric Point 3 · Constant of Integration with Initial Condition (1 pt): Substitute \(x = 0, y = 3\): \[ \ln|3 - 1| = \frac{0}{4} + C \implies C = \ln(2). \]

Rubric Point 4 · Explicit Solution for \(y\) (1 pt): Exponentiate both sides: \[ |y - 1| = e^{x^2/4 + \ln 2} = 2e^{x^2/4}. \] Since \(y(0) = 3 > 1\), \(|y - 1| = y - 1\): \[ \mathbf{y = 1 + 2e^{x^2/4}}. \]

Result: 5 out of 5 points earned with zero point deduction.
body.ar:
FRQ Prompt: Consider the المعادلة التفاضلية \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{x(y - 1)}{2}\) with initial condition \(y(0) = 3\). أوجد particular الحل \(y = f(x)\).

Rubric Point 1 · Separation of المتغيرات (1 pt): \[ \frac{1}{y - 1}\,dy = \frac{x}{2}\,dx. \]

Rubric Point 2 · Antiderivatives (2 pts): 1 pt for left side, 1 pt for right side: \[ \ln|y - 1| = \frac{x^2}{4} + C. \]

Rubric Point 3 · الثابت of Integration with Initial Condition (1 pt): عوّض \(x = 0, y = 3\): \[ \ln|3 - 1| = \frac{0}{4} + C \implies C = \ln(2). \]

Rubric Point 4 · Explicit الحل for \(y\) (1 pt): Exponentiate both sides: \[ |y - 1| = e^{x^2/4 + \ln 2} = 2e^{x^2/4}. \] Since \(y(0) = 3 > 1\), \(|y - 1| = y - 1\): \[ \mathbf{y = 1 + 2e^{x^2/4}}. \]

Result: 5 out of 5 points earned with zero point deduction.

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced / AP FRQ

On an AP Calculus BC exam question asking whether a series \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n\) converges, a student writes: "Since \(\lim_{n\to\infty} a_n = 0\), the series converges." Evaluate the mathematical validity of this statement, identify the logical fallacy, and provide a standard counterexample that disproves it.
question.ar:
Level 3 · Advanced / AP FRQ

On an AP Calculus BC exam question asking whether a series \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n\) converges, a student writes: "Since \(\lim_{n\to\infty} a_n = 0\), the series converges." احسب قيمة the mathematical validity of this statement, identإذا كانy the logical fallacy, and provide a standard counterexample that disproves it.

solution.en:
Evaluation: The statement is mathematically invalid and earns 0 points.

Logical Fallacy: The student has committed the fallacy of the converse. The \(n\)-th Term Test states: If a series \(\sum a_n\) converges, then \(\lim_{n\to\infty} a_n = 0\). The contrapositive is also true: If \(\lim_{n\to\infty} a_n eq 0\), then the series diverges. However, \(\lim_{n\to\infty} a_n = 0\) is a necessary condition, NOT a sufficient condition for convergence.

Counterexample: The harmonic series \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{n}\). Here \(\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{n} = 0\), yet the harmonic series is a \(p\)-series with \(p = 1\), which diverges to infinity.

question.en: [Practice 4 · Hard] Consider the sequence \( a_n = \frac{1}{n!} \int_0^n e^{-t^2} dt \). Which of the following statements about the convergence of \( \lbrace a_n \rbrace \) is true?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (AP Calculus BC Exam Format & Units Overview): [Practice 4 · Hard] Consider the sequence \( a_n = \frac{1}{n!} \int_0^n e^{-t^2} dt \). Which of the following statements about the convergence of \( \lbrace a_n \rbrace \) is true?

hints.en: Let \( I_n = \int_0^n e^{-t^2} dt \). We know that \( e^{-t^2} \le 1 \) for all \( t \ge 0 \). Thus, \( I_n = \int_0^n e^{-t^2} dt \le \int_0^n 1 dt = n \). More precisely, as \( n \to \infty \), \( I_n \) approaches \( \int_0^\infty e^{-t^2} dt = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2} \), which is a finite constant. Therefore, \( I_n \) is bounded.
hints.ar: ليكن \( I_n = \int_0^n e^{-t^2} dt \). We know that \( e^{-t^2} \le 1 \) for all \( t \ge 0 \). وعليه، \( I_n = \int_0^n e^{-t^2} dt \le \int_0^n 1 dt = n \). More precisely, as \( n \to \infty \), \( I_n \) approaches \( \int_0^\infty e^{-t^2} dt = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2} \), which is a finite constant. وبالتالي، \( I_n \) is bounded.

hints.en: Now consider the sequence \( a_n = \frac{I_n}{n!} \). We have \( 0 \le a_n = \frac{I_n}{n!} \le \frac{n}{n!} = \frac{1}{(n-1)!} \) for \( n \ge 1 \).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( a_n = \frac{I_n}{n!} \) ، \( 0 \le a_n = \frac{I_n}{n!} \le \frac{n}{n!} = \frac{1}{(n-1)!} \) ، \( n \ge 1 \) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: We know that \(\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{(n-1)!} = 0\). By the Squeeze Theorem, since \(0 \le a_n \le \frac{1}{(n-1)!}\) and \(\lim_{n\to\infty} 0 = 0\) and \(\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{(n-1)!} = 0\), we can conclude that \(\lim_{n\to\infty} a_n\). Thus, the sequence converges to 0.
hints.ar: We know that \(\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{(n-1)!} = 0\). بتطبيق Squeeze Theorem, since \(0 \le a_n \le \frac{1}{(n-1)!}\) and \(\lim_{n\to\infty} 0 = 0\) and \(\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{(n-1)!} = 0\), we can conclude that \(\lim_{n\to\infty} a_n\). وعليه، the sequence converges to 0.

question.en: Consider the function represented by the graph of \( f(x) \) below. What is the value of the definite integral \( \int_{0}^{4} f(x) \, dx \)?
question.ar: Consider the function represented بتطبيق graph of \( f(x) \) below. ما قيمة the definite integral \( \int_{0}^{4} f(x) \, dx \)?

hints.en: The definite integral \( \int_{0}^{4} f(x) \, dx \) represents the area under the curve \( f(x) \) from \( x=0 \) to \( x=4 \).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( \int_{0}^{4} f(x) \, dx \) ، \( f(x) \) ، \( x=0 \) ، \( x=4 \) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: The graph of \( f(x) \) from \( x=0 \) to \( x=4 \) forms a triangle with a base of 4 units (from 0 to 4 on the x-axis) and a height of 6 units (the value of \( f(x) \) at \( x=0 \)). The area of a triangle is given by \( \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} \).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( f(x) \) ، \( x=0 \) ، \( x=4 \) ، \( f(x) \) ، \( x=0 \) ، \( \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} \) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en: The definite integral \( \int_{0}^{4} f(x) \, dx \) represents the area under the curve \( f(x) \) from \( x=0 \) to \( x=4 \). The graph of \( f(x) \) from \( x=0 \) to \( x=4 \) forms a triangle with a base of 4 units (from 0 to 4 on the x-axis) and a height of 6 units (the value of \( f(x) \) at \( x=0 \)). The area of a triangle is given by \( \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} \). Therefore, the area is \( \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 6 = 12 \).
